text:
The court should most likely apply Washington law and deny the punitive damages claim. A federal court sitting in diversity applies Washington's choice-of-law rules, and Washington's public policy against punitive damages (see *Dailey v. North Coast Life Ins. Co.*, 129 Wn.2d 572 (1996), cited from memory and not re-checked) generally keeps them out even where the injury occurred. Both options in the team note point to California, which I think is wrong: there is no federal common law of punitive damages in a diversity case, and Washington replaced lex loci with the most-significant-relationship test for torts.

CONFIDENCE: 40
